title: Factor thickenings of a specified split reduction
statement: Let A and R be commutative rings and R an A-algebra with R modulo its nilradical isomorphic as A-algebra to a finite product of A-algebras D_i. There are pairwise disjoint opens W_i covering Spec R, and surjective closed immersions Spec D_i into W_i, whose composites to Spec A are the structural morphisms of D_i. This includes an empty index set.

source.place: Proof, finite-algebra calculation: after the reduced tensor algebra is split, take factor spectra and lift their open-and-closed components through reduction.

proof.text: For the quotient map q: Spec(R/nilradical R) -> Spec R, use Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective and PrimeSpectrum.comap_quotientMk_bijective_of_le_nilradical to obtain an embedding and surjectivity. Thus q is a homeomorphism by isHomeomorph_iff_isEmbedding_surjective. Compose it with PrimeSpectrum.homeomorphOfRingEquiv for the supplied algebra equivalence and PrimeSpectrum.sigmaToPiHomeo D. This explicitly gives a homeomorphism H from the disjoint union of the factor prime spectra to Spec R, whose restriction to factor i is Spec of eval_i composed with the equivalence and quotient.

Set W_i to the range of the factor map g_i. Under H this is the image of the open range of Sigma.mk i, so it is open by isOpenMap_sigmaMk and H.isOpenMap. Surjectivity of H proves the supremum of these opens is top; injectivity of H and equality of sigma first coordinates prove pairwise disjointness. The same argument works when the index type is empty and when factors are zero rings.

The composite ring map k_i: R -> D_i is surjective, so g_i is a closed immersion by Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective. Apply IsOpenImmersion.lift to the open inclusion W_i -> Spec R and g_i, whose range is W_i. The factorization identity and the definition of W_i show the lift a_i is surjective. IsPreimmersion.of_comp gives that a_i is a preimmersion, and its range is the whole target, a closed set. Apply IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion. Finally rewrite the structural-map composite with Spec.map_comp and check equality of ring maps on elements using e.commutes and the quotient algebra structure.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_split_reduction_factor_thickenings
    (A R : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [Algebra A R]
    (r : ℕ) (D : Fin r → Type u) [∀ j, CommRing (D j)] [∀ j, Algebra A (D j)]
    (he : Nonempty ((R ⧸ _root_.nilradical R) ≃ₐ[A] (∀ j, D j))) :
    ∃ (W : Fin r → (Spec (.of R)).Opens),
      (⨆ i, W i) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (W i) (W j)) ∧
      ∀ i, ∃ (a : Spec (.of (D i)) ⟶ (W i).toScheme),
        IsClosedImmersion a ∧ Surjective a ∧
          a ≫ (W i).ι ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A R)) =
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (D i)))
